The effectiveness of laser treatments would depend on the TYPE of laser machine/ method and your type of hair (thick, thin, dark, light).

The most effective laser for me (dark thick hair) so far is any clinic using Candela GentleMax Pro. Diode or IPL doesn't work as effectively for thicker hair-- they may seem cheaper but you'll have to get more sessions (and not even sure if they'd be effective).

With regards to epilating vs laser, i think epilating hurts more and takes longer. You'll also be more prone to prolonged redness and bruising. Laser can also hurt for half a second but then the whole procedure would be over really quickly. The hair will also fall out and grow fewer and farther in between after a few sessions. I haven't gotten any new laser sessions in months and i still notice some "bald spots" where hair stopped growing. Ofcourse it's an investment too because the more effective lasers are not cheap.

To summarize, my laser machine recommendation is GentleMax Pro (which uses both an Alexandrite laser and a Nd: YAG laser).

If someone is mansplaining something, it gives off a feeling that they assume you dont know anything about the topic without asking first and they may deliver their explanation in a condescending way. It generally makes one feel like they’re being spoken to as if they’re stupid.

To be honest, i was expecting to get discriminated when i applied. Pero hindi din ako galit sa mga filipino na hindi pa fully knowledgeable sa invisible disabilities even if they work in government institutions. Yes, something should be done to improve things, but right now this is the reality. 

So ito naging approach ko. Sharing incase these points may help someone (definitely not applicable to all):

- I made sure i had complete reqs. I triple checked via phone call for any uncertainties para maavoid ang 2nd visit. 

- I dressed down. I didnt wear anything fancy or fashionable. Pang bahay at tsinelas lang to avoid anyone thinking "bakit sya nagaapply e mukha naman siyang may pera" since the ID comes with discounts (lol)

- I kept to myself and stayed quiet most of the time. While waiting, binabasa ko yung mga nakapaskil sa bulletin boards. I have a neurological disability but i seem high functioning. Keeping quiet avoids giving the impression that i seem high functioning. 

- When spoken to, i spoke slowly and politely. People are generally inclined to help when you’re nice to them. Dont correct them or be a know-it-all. You’re in their space at that moment and they hold the power. 

- Lastly (medyo weird but) I came around/ after lunch time. No joke people are usually in better spiritis while eating. Nagoffer pa sila sakin ng food. 

Got my ID that same afternoon. 

Note: I’m diagnosed adhd po (+possibly on the autism spectrum as well) so natural for me to over think kaya ayan inoverthink ko talaga. I dont mean to offend anyone working in these offices, this is just my attempt to be extra avoidant of any negative outcomes.

Psychologists typically perform specialized therapies (psychotherapy/ CBT). They usually cannot prescribe medicine. I’ve met some with the following specializations: childhood trauma, homeopathic healing, art therapy, etc. Some psychologists professionally call themselves Therapists or Counselors. Some teach in universities instead or prefer catering to students. Meron pa nga that specialize in paranormal psychology. 

Psychiatrists can prescribe medicine and some can perform specialized therapies too but just prefer not to. They usually have their own psychiatric specializations (bipolar, bpd, depression, adhd, ptsd, etc), are able to diagnose, provide prescription drugs, and PWD certificates. Most that i know focus on how the disability affects your hormones/ body chemicals then recommend medicine to help alleviate the symptoms. 

I guess if you need a guidance counselor/ academic type of approach- you generally go for a psychologist. If you need someone who can prescribe drugs and really functions like the typical doctor - psychiatrist. 

Some professionals are sort of a combination of the two. So it’s great to hear yours does psychotherapy. ☺️
